name: Vicente Gonzalez
page_title: Vicente Gonzalez's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (TX) - District 34

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "Increase funding for critical health care and family planning services for women."
Voted in favor of HR 3755 "Women's Health Protection Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 8296 "Women's Health Protection Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "Congressman Gonzalez opposes ill-advised efforts to privatize Social Security or turn Medicare into a voucher system. The Congressman supports protecting and expanding Social Security and Medicare for all Americans."

"For decades, Medicare and Social Security have helped millions of Americans retire comfortably after a lifetime of work. As a country, we made a promise to protect our elderly and ensure they would have reliable access to the resources and support that they earned. Now more than ever, we cannot abandon our seniors when their resources, and ultimately their independence is threatened."

"The Congressman has proudly co-sponsored legislation that would address the long-term challenges associated with funding Social Security and ensure that seniors' hard-earned benefits keep pace with the rising cost of living, healthcare, and prescription drugs. Some of this legislation includes H.R. 82, the Social Security Fairness Act, which eliminates the windfall elimination provision, and H.R. 5376, the Inflation Reduction Act, which provides savings on prescription drugs and limits insulin to $35 a month for seniors on Medicare."
Rated 100% by National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare (NCPSM

positions.question: Do you support a decrease in income taxes in order to balance the budget?

evidence.text: "Congressman Gonzalez is a voice for American consumers and an advocate for fiscally responsible policies that encourage economic growth and job creation in South Texas. He supports updating our nation's tax regime so that all Americans benefit from the nation's tax system equitably. He also supports reducing barriers for folks entering and moving up in the workforce, such as lowering the cost of education and increasing access to childcare."
"The so called "FairTax" plan would hurt middle class families and slash taxes for the ultra-wealthy. South Texans won’t be fooled."
Rated 11% by National Taxpayers Union

positions.question: Do you support protecting government officials, including law enforcement officers, from personal liability in civil lawsuits concerning alleged misconduct?

evidence.text: "Increase investments and resources for local law enforcement and first responders."

"We are seeing, now more than ever, the critical need to reform our policing system and its officers. It's not about defunding, but about making substantial changes to training methods that impact the way policing happens in America. We need to promote a system that encourages and rewards good officers for taking a stand against bad officers who hurt the reputation of all police in America. We need to raise accountability and provide additional racial and bias training for police. Independent review boards, body cameras, and using violence as a last resort to de-escalate situations are just a few places we can start to make change."
Vote in favor of HR 1280 "George Floyd Justice in Policing Act of 2021"

positions.question: Do you support increasing defense spending?

evidence.text: "America is the land of the free, and I support a strong military and national defense to ensure we stay that way. Today we face various enemies who play by different rules, and we must stay vigilant while honoring the Constitutional rights of US citizens. As Congressman, I will support the critical efforts to keep our country and families safe."
"Keeping our military strong and continuing to remain a leading force in global defense and protection."
Voted in favor of HR 2670 "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024"
Voted in favor of HR 7900 "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023"

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "South Texas lacks a major highway connecting us to the rest of the state and the nation. With the enactment of the bipartisan infrastructure bill we are steps closer to completing projects like I-69 and improving our infrastructure connectivity."

"Today, I voted to pass the bipartisan infrastructure bill and send it to the President's desk. This legislation will create good-paying jobs, invest in our roads, bridges, dams, and broadband, and ensure our south Texas communities are equipped to succeed and compete globally. This critical investment in our crumbling infrastructure is long overdue. We must continue bringing transformational change to all and assure working families have a fair shot."
Voted in favor of HR 3684 "Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act"
Voted in favor of HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "#FairHousing means ensuring that everyone, no matter who they are, has access to safe, decent, and affordable housing, so that they can thrive. #FairHousingMonth"
"Great to meet everyone and discuss solutions to housing in South Texas!"
"Housing is a basic human right, not a privilege. We should all be able to own a home. #OurHomesOurVoices"
"To invest in the future of our communities, we must invest in safe and affordable housing in every zip code. #OurHomesOurVoices"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "The Inflation Reduction Act is an important opportunity to counteract inflation and deliver for South Texas. It is far from perfect, but it is the product of compromise. The bill caps the cost of insulin, sets an out-of-pocket cap on and lowers the price of medication for medicare beneficiaries, reduces energy and healthcare costs for South Texas families and requires corporations and those at the top to pay their fair share in taxes without raising taxes on families making $400,000 or less."

"The Inflation Reduction Act is historic legislation that will lower kitchen table costs, dramatically reduce the deficit and support our seniors without raising taxes for middle class American families and small businesses."
Voted in favor of HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"
Voted in favor of HR 7688 "Consumer Fuel Price Gouging Prevention Act"

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "Help our college students graduate debt free."

"Student borrowers across the country and in Texas are struggling under the crushing burden of $1.5 trillion in student loans. President Biden can lift this burden with a stroke of a pen by permanently canceling their student loan debt. There's no time to waste."
"We can do more than pause loans, we can wipe them away. It’s time to #CancelStudentDebt, and my bill, the Student Loan Relief Act, can be the first step."

"Of the 45 million Americans who hold student debt, 1 in 5 are over 50 years old…in an era of declining wages and rising debt, Americans are not aging out of their student loans—they are aging into them." @potus it is time to #CancelStudentDebt"

positions.question: Do you support requiring a government-issued identification in order to vote at the polls?

evidence.text: "The right to vote is an indispensable pillar in the foundation of our democracy. I commend the Texas legislators who had the courage to leave their families, homes, jobs and the great state of Texas to preserve our democracy. The U.S. House of Representatives has done its part to advance voting rights legislation by passing H.R. 1, the For the People Act. President Biden must take a stand and urge the Senate to do whatever is necessary to pass critical legislation that maintains the integrity of our elections and protects every American's sacred right to vote."

"Today, I proudly voted for #HR4, the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to #RestoreTheVote. It is important we protect this sacred right that heroes like John Lewis fought so bravely to protect."
Voted in favor of HR 4 "John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 5746 "Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act"

positions.question: Do you support government funding for the development of renewable energy (e.g. solar, wind, geo-thermal)?

evidence.text: "Congressman Gonzalez also supports the development of sources of renewable energy, acknowledging the potential in wind and solar energy for both the South Texas economy and American energy independence. Currently, Texas produces more wind energy than most other U.S. states. The 34th District is home to part of the Los Vientos Wind farm, the second largest wind farm in the country."

"Congressman Gonzalez supports an all-the-above approach to energy and understands the importance of American energy not only to power our cars and homes, but also as a national security issue and a job creator."

"Many have raised concerns with provisions pertaining to domestic energy production. Rest assured that I worked and am still working to assure this bill does not prevent the United States from leading the world in responsible oil and gas production. This legislation will empower us to invest in the technologies to create a cleaner, greener future. I look forward to continuing my work to bring energy costs down for all Americans and ensure the United States remains energy independent."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government allowing permits for drilling on public lands?

evidence.text: "As chairman of the Congressional Oil and Gas Caucus, Congressman Gonzalez aims to bring a Texas perspective to Washington, D.C., regarding the oil and gas industry. The leads the caucus as an opportunity to educate fellow lawmakers about the production and distribution of oil, gas and other petroleum hydrocarbons, including crude oil, natural gas and gas liquids."

"Congressman Gonzalez also supports the development of sources of renewable energy, acknowledging the potential in wind and solar energy for both the South Texas economy and American energy independence. Currently, Texas produces more wind energy than most other U.S. states. The 34th District is home to part of the Los Vientos Wind farm, the second largest wind farm in the country."
"Thank you @potus for banning Russian oil imports. Now is the time to unleash American energy production to support hardworking Americans and our allies."

"Due to current regulations, offshore wind leases cannot move forward until offshore oil and gas leases are offered by the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM). It’s imperative that BOE finalize the five-year program and hold uninterrupted lease sales immediately so America’s burgeoning offshore wind sector can flourish. This sector will create tens of thousands of jobs over the next few years and drastically improve our country’s energy security by harnessing non-traditional energy sources to power our homes, schools, and businesses. What’s more, offshore wind is poised to be a significant contributor to our environmental restoration efforts — with the potential to invest millions into coastal restoration and outdoor recreation initiatives. For this to work, offshore oil and gas lease sales must be held in a timely manner."

positions.question: Do you generally support gun-control legislation (e.g. red flag laws, boyfriend loopholes)?

evidence.text: Voted in favor of HR 1446 "Enhanced Background Checks Act of 2021"

"Mayra Flores is too dangerous for South Texas families. In Congress, Mayra has: Voted AGAINST Senator Cornyn’s bipartisan gun control bill that increases school safety measures and protects women in abusive relationships. We can’t let Mayra win in November."

"My thoughts and prayers today are with the victims of the tragic #OdessaShooting. We need to pass universal background checks, gun safety legislation and other common sense reforms or we will continue on this path."

"This inaction must stop. We know background checks save lives. Every day background checks stop more than 170 felons and 50 domestic abusers from getting a gun. Any delay to pass commonsense gun violence prevention legislation only increases the chances that more innocent people in America may suffer from the tragic and needless loss caused by gun violence. Again, we urge you to follow the leadership of the House Democratic Majority and immediately come back into session to pass H.R 8, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act and H.R. 1112, the Enhanced Background Checks Act, that could prevent dangerous criminals from obtaining weapons and save lives."

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "12 yrs ago today, Pres. Obama signed the #AffordableCareAct into law making healthcare more affordable for millions of Americans. Last year, the #AmericanRescuePlan made coverage more affordable for thousands of Texans. Now, we must cont. working to expand access & lower costs."

"All South Texans deserve access to affordable, quality health care, including those who live in rural communities and medically underserved areas. Unfortunately, South Texas is home to a large uninsured or underinsured population. Congressman Gonzalez continues to work with his colleagues to develop innovative ideas that lower health care costs and provide better coverage for more people."
"Strengthen and improve the Affordable Care Act."

"The Congressman recognizes that more needs to be done to lower premiums, expand coverage, and improve the Affordable Care Act. While the Affordable Care Act was a step in the right direction, he understands it is not perfect. For these reasons, he supports working across the aisle to build consensus and develop common sense solutions to improve our health care systems."

positions.question: Do you support expanding paid family AND/OR medical leave benefits (e.g. maternity leave)?

evidence.text: "As of 2015, only 12% of U.S. private sector workers had access to paid family leave through their employer. I support workplace rights because they allow our nation’s economy to grow and provide essential care to newborns in their first months of life."

"Not only does paid maternity leave have immense benefits on child health outcomes, but it can also increase female labor force participation by allowing women to stay in the workforce after giving birth."
"That means making child care more affordable, standing by family medical leave, and ensuring that affordable health care is within the reach of every working Texan."

"We lead the world in many ways, but we are woefully behind when it comes to taking care of hardworking families. There is no reason that of the 195 countries, we are part of the eight that don’t offer national paid family leave. We must do better."

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

"Lower prescription drug prices."

"New $2,000 Out-Of-Pocket Cap for Part D Drugs for Seniors on Medicare: Caps Part D out-of-pocket drug costs at $2,000 a year for seniors and individuals with disabilities on Medicare, starting in 2025. Caps Insulin Costs at $35 A Month for Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities on Medicare: Caps Medicare beneficiaries' insulin costs at $35 a month. Republicans voted against capping insulin out-of-pockets costs for Americans with private health insurance keeping this vital protection out of the bill."
